calls.reason: A September 2025 paper by Kalai and colleagues says hallucinations still persist even in state-of-the-art systems. The packet holds nothing showing they were eliminated, so his present-tense claim that they aren't going away has held up so far.

The only evidence is the November 2024 SimpleQA paper, which shows model factuality limits but has no matched human-expert baseline. A possibly contrary physician study could not be read, so the end-2024 milestone can't be called either way.

The Cisco survey and the Morris II worm paper support the security and concern parts. But the packet has no matched financial evidence on whether generative AI was making much money, so the main composite claim stays unsettled.

The a16z research shows models converging and buyers designing for easy switching, and OpenAI cut prices. But the same research notes cloud-provider and feature advantages, and nothing ties the price cuts to competition rather than lower costs.

The WSJ report traces the $50B-vs-$3B figures to a Sequoia estimate, but their coverage isn't reconciled. Sequoia's own analysis expects costs to fall, so 'obviously not sustainable' is a judgment the evidence doesn't settle.
